symptom: ako/mxcli#1563: `describe page` printed a combo box with custom content as if it had none (`combobox cbBooking (… optionsSourceAssociationCustomContentType: 'yes')`), so the widgets in it — txtOptionName, bound to Booking.Name — were visible to nobody until mx check named one. A `create or modify` of that description that CHANGES the combo box drops the content (Replaced page, then CE0642 'Custom content is required'); unchanged, the pluggable passthrough keeps it
cause: The NOT SHOWN note for a child slot holding widgets (unreconstructedContainers, #965) is computed only for generic pluggable widgets; a combo box is a known type with its own describer, and MDL cannot author its custom content (MDL-WIDGET26), so nothing ever said it was there
fix: A combo box whose widgets properties hold widgets is described with a `-- NOT SHOWN:` comment before it, naming the property and each widget (or 'an unnamed <kind>'), what keeps and what loses the content, and `alter page … set` as the edit that keeps it. The output still parses and re-executes; GetPut on the repro page stays 'Unchanged page'
test: TestDescribeComboBoxNamesItsHiddenCustomContent (the shipped template plus content; reparses), control TestDescribeComboBoxWithoutCustomContentHasNoNote
insight: Measure what a note claims before writing it: on 11.13.0 the content survives describe → exec in place only while the combo box is unchanged (passthrough), is lost when the statement changes it (CE0642), and `alter … set` keeps it — three outcomes the generic note's 'Re-running this script would DROP it … re-add the block by hand' gets wrong for a widget whose block cannot be written at all. The note names widgets rather than the slot keyword because the name is what the replace refusal and `drop` take
